hypothesis: LiTaF6 is the next coating to evaluate. It has the lowest frozen penalty among the unevaluated candidates (0.027, bin 1, acceptable) and a 5.9 eV gap. LiNbF6, the structural and chemical analogue (same fluoride framework, similar cation size), gave a weaker electrolyte contact of about 1.63 J/m2 and a cathode contact of about 3.6 J/m2. I expect LiTaF6 to show a similar pattern, with the electrolyte contact as the bottleneck. This is a prediction from one analogue, not a computed value. LiCaAlF6 has a higher penalty (bin 2) and is second. LiF is thermodynamically rejected (bin 15), so adhesion cannot rescue it and it stays last.
change_trigger: Revisit the ranking if the validated LiTaF6 electrolyte W_adh falls below about 1.4 J/m2 or rises above about 1.9 J/m2, if the weaker contact flips to the cathode, or if the penalty bin or acceptance changes on re-evaluation. A LiCaAlF6 result with a higher min(W_adh) at its penalty bin 2 would also justify promoting it.
